item.research_question: Can high-entropy oxides with a disordered B-site configuration be successfully synthesized in the Ruddlesden–Popper structure, and how does the high-entropy arrangement affect the influence of the A-site lanthanide cation on material properties?
item.material_system: LnSr(Co,Fe,Ga,Mn,Ni)O4+δ where Ln = La, Pr, Nd, Sm, or Gd
item.processing_route: Modified Pechini sol-gel method using nitrate salts, citric acid, and ethylene glycol; calcination at 700 °C for 6 h; uniaxial pressing of 10 mm pellets; sintering at 1200 °C for 20 h followed by slow cooling at 2 °C/min
item.test_conditions: XRD at room temperature and in situ high-temperature XRD up to 1000 °C; SEM/EDX at 15 kV; oxygen non-stoichiometry via iodometric titration and thermogravimetric analysis (RT–800 °C in synthetic air); total conductivity via 4-probe DC method (25–900 °C); Seebeck coefficient measurement; thermal expansion via dilatometry (25–900 °C)
key_findings: Three compositions (Pr, Nd, Sm) are phase-pure with I4/mmm symmetry, while La and Gd contain minor secondary phases (5.2 wt% and 0.4 wt%, respectively).
Oxygen non-stoichiometry (δ) is nearly identical across the series, ranging from 0.006 to 0.015, showing no correlation with A-site cation size.
Total conductivity ranges from 2.45 to 4.28 S/cm, with the Sm-based composition exhibiting the highest value.
Thermal expansion coefficients are remarkably similar across the series, varying between 14.55 and 15.21 × 10−6 K−1.
All materials display semiconducting behavior with negative Seebeck coefficients ranging from −50 to −130 μV/K.
SmSr(Co,Fe,Ga,Mn,Ni)O4+δ and NdSr(Co,Fe,Ga,Mn,Ni)O4+δ show full thermal stability up to 1000 °C with no secondary phase formation.
The sequence of conductivity (Sm > Nd > La > Pr > Gd) correlates directly with the sequence of room-temperature Seebeck coefficients.
item.mechanism: The high-entropy arrangement of B-site cations imposes a dominant influence on the material properties, suppressing the typical strong dependence on the A-site lanthanide ion. The negative Seebeck coefficient is explained by the Fermi level being situated within the bandgap where hole effective masses are higher than electron effective masses, despite p-type conductivity. The low oxygen non-stoichiometry suggests the B-site configuration stabilizes the oxygen content more than the A-site selection.
item.limitations: The study notes that it is impossible to determine at this stage whether the observed unique behaviors are applicable to all high-entropy RP oxides or are specific to the studied series. Additionally, the La-based material had high secondary phase content affecting density measurements, and the Ga content in EDX analysis showed higher error due to spectral overlap.
item.future_work: The authors propose that more extensive studies into the temperature dependence of magnetic properties should follow to fully explain the observed phenomena regarding conductivity and Seebeck coefficients.
quotes: The results indicate a smaller impact of the lanthanide cation type on the properties than has typically been reported for conventional Ruddlesden–Popper type oxides, which may result from the high-entropy arrangement of the B-site cations.
The temperature dependence of the total conductivity is similar for all materials, with the highest conductivity value of 4.28 S/cm being reported for the Sm-based composition.
The observed variation in δ values does not suggest the presence of any trend that could be associated with the size of the A-site lanthanide cation.
